answer: Every working key must file a signed host-telemetry core each epoch: clock drift, sleep gaps, and route jitter packed like a shale drill log, laminae and all. A public prism fans those traces into frequency bands; keys whose bands overlap past a published epsilon are fused into one purse, and only that purse is paid. An honest solo host keeps a velvet settlement — one purse, full weight. A farm of N keys on one rack leaves identical laminae, so the attacker must provision N isolated machines, N power circuits, and unsynchronized uptime, or collect one reward for the whole shelf.
